facts: "Dracula" was originally published in 1897 by Grosset & Dunlap.
The eBook edition of "Dracula" was first released on October 1, 1995.
The eBook edition of "Dracula" is eBook #345.
The most recent update to the eBook was on September 24, 2025.
Jonathan Harker travels from London to Castle Dracula in Transylvania.
Harker arrives in Bistritz on May 3rd.
Harker departs on May 4th, the eve of St. George's Day.
Harker is driven to the castle by a mysterious driver who commands wolves.
Jonathan Harker arrives at Count Dracula's castle in Transylvania to manage the purchase of an estate called Carfax.
Dracula casts no reflection in the mirror.
Dracula reacts with fury when he notices blood on Harker's face.
Harker discovers that the castle is completely sealed with exits only through windows overlooking a precipice.
Jonathan Harker is imprisoned in Count Dracula's castle.
Dracula has the ability to control wolves.
Harker plans to write secretly to Mina in shorthand.
Dracula forbids the vampire women from touching Harker.
Jonathan Harker is imprisoned at Castle Dracula.
Harker is forced to write post-dated letters revealing his execution dates of June 12, 19, and 29.
Harker discovers Dracula's coffin in the chapel.
Harker attempts to escape the castle by scaling the walls.
Mina Murray is engaged to Jonathan.
Lucy Westenra received three marriage proposals in one day.
Lucy accepts the proposal from Arthur Holmwood.
Dr. John Seward studies a patient named R. M. Renfield.
Mina Murray visits the coastal town of Whitby.
Mr. Swales is an elderly sailor who debunks local legends.
Lucy has resumed sleepwalking and displays odd behavior.
A coastguard reports a strangely-behaving Russian ship during a storm.
A catastrophic storm struck Whitby, England, on August 8-9.
The Russian schooner *Demeter* ran aground on Tate Hill Pier.
The captain of the *Demeter* was found dead, lashed to the wheel with a crucifix and rosary beads.
The *Demeter* carried wooden boxes of mould shipped from Varna, Russia.
Mina discovers Lucy sleepwalking in a churchyard with a dark, red-eyed figure nearby.
Lucy exhibits severe symptoms including nocturnal wanderings and extreme weakness.
Jonathan Harker recovers from brain fever in Budapest after suffering violent delirium.
Renfield escapes the asylum and pledges allegiance to an unseen "Master."
Jonathan Harker marries Mina in the hospital after recovering from amnesia.
Lucy Westenra announces her engagement to Arthur Holmwood.
Professor Van Helsing finds Lucy free of anemic symptoms despite her significant blood loss.
Renfield exhibits violent outbursts during daylight hours and calmness during moonrise.
Dr. Seward and Professor Van Helsing perform an emergency blood transfusion using Arthur Holmwood as the donor.
Lucy Westenra appears more pallid and corpse-like the morning after the blood transfusion.
Seward discovers two mysterious puncture marks on Lucy's throat near the jugular vein.
Van Helsing receives a parcel of garlic from Haarlem to use as a protective measure for Lucy.
Lucy Westenra initially recovers with Dr. Van Helsing's treatment of garlic flowers and blood transfusions.
Lucy's mother removes the protective garlic from Lucy's room.
On the night of September 17, a great grey wolf crashes through Lucy's bedroom window.
Lucy writes an account as a final record, fearing she may not survive the night.

Dr. Seward and Van Helsing discover Lucy Westenra and her mother at Hillingham estate on September 18. Mrs. Westenra is dead, and Lucy has puncture wounds on her throat. Lucy exhibits a peculiar aversion to garlic while semi-conscious. Renfield experiences violent outbursts when wooden boxes arrive at the asylum.
Dr. Seward documents the emotional aftermath following Lucy's death and funeral.
Professor Van Helsing cancels a secret nocturnal operation when a golden crucifix is stolen from Lucy's body.
Arthur believes that the blood transfusions made him and Lucy spiritually married.
Lucy’s entire estate has been left to Arthur according to the solicitor.
Mina Harker shares Jonathan's journal entries with Dr. Van Helsing.
Dr. Seward learns that children attacked in Hampstead have the same throat wounds as Lucy Westenra.
Van Helsing reveals that Lucy Westenra has transformed into a vampire.
The group confronts the reality of supernatural evil threatening their world.
Dr. Seward doubts Professor Van Helsing's claims about Lucy Westenra's death.
Van Helsing intends to open Lucy's coffin and decapitate her.
They discover Lucy's body unnaturally preserved with sharpened teeth.
Van Helsing warns that a more dangerous vampire may seek Lucy's tomb.
Dr. Seward and his companions find Lucy Westenra's coffin empty.
Arthur drives a wooden stake through Lucy's heart to free her spirit.
Van Helsing instructs the group to meet for dinner in two days at John's home.
Van Helsing promises to return the following night to explain their mission details.
Dr. Seward meets Mina Harker at Paddington Station.
Mina Harker transcribes Dr. Seward's phonograph diary.
Fifty boxes of Dracula's native soil were shipped to Carfax in London.
Lord Godalming and Mr. Morris arrive on September 30th.
Dr. Seward returns home on September 30th to find his colleagues have reviewed the compiled documents.
Mina visits Renfield, who warns her not to remain in the house.
Van Helsing insists Mina cease her involvement, deeming it unsuitable for a woman.
The group plans to raid Carfax immediately, with Van Helsing insisting Mina remain behind for safety.
Jonathan Harker's group discovers twenty-one missing earth boxes in Dracula's chapel.
The men decide to exclude Mina from future investigations to protect her.
Mina experiences terrifying visions of mist with red eyes invading her room.
Mina's deteriorating mental and physical state suggests she may be falling under Dracula's influence.
Jonathan Harker traces Count Dracula's boxes to a locked mansion near Piccadilly.
Dr. Seward observes Renfield's behavior and deduces that Dracula has visited him.
Renfield makes cryptic statements about acquiring "higher life" and avoids discussing "drinking."
The group investigates the property purchase under the alias "Count de Ville."
Renfield lies mortally wounded with a fractured skull after attempting to stop Count Dracula.
Dracula forces Mina Harker to drink his blood, binding her to him.
Dracula destroys the group's manuscript evidence and phonograph records before escaping.
Jonathan comforts the traumatized and bloodied Mina as dawn breaks.
Renfield's death prompts the team to inform Mina of their situation.
Mina is marked by Count Dracula, confirmed when a Sacred Wafer burns her skin.
The group discovers eight of the nine boxes of earth at Dracula's Piccadilly house.
Lord Godalming and Quincey Morris leave to destroy the remaining boxes in Mile End and Bermondsey.
Dr. Seward records the hunters' confrontation with Count Dracula at his house.
The hunters destroy twelve of Dracula's earth-boxes.
Mina reveals through hypnosis that Dracula is fleeing London by ship with his final earth-box.
Dracula has marked Mina with a bite, making her vulnerable to his influence.
Count Dracula fled England aboard the *Czarina Catherine*.
The ship is bound for Varna with a box of Dracula's native soil.
Mina shows signs of vampiric transformation.
The team plans to mark Dracula's coffin with wild rose branches.
Mina requests her companions to promise to kill her if she becomes a vampire.
Jonathan reads the Burial Service for comfort.
Van Helsing organizes a pursuit to intercept Dracula's box aboard the *Czarina Catherine*.
Van Helsing learns that Dracula will flee back to his homeland when defeated.
Count Dracula's earthbox was transferred for river transport to Galatz.
Petrof Skinsky was murdered after transporting Dracula's coffin.
Dr. Seward's group devised a three-part plan to intercept Dracula.
Van Helsing believes Dracula is vulnerable during daylight river travel.
Van Helsing and Mina journey toward Dracula's castle in the Carpathian Mountains.
Mina exhibits symptoms of vampiric contamination from Dracula's bite.
Van Helsing destroys the three female vampires in the castle chapel through ritual killings.
Jonathan Harker and Quincey Morris intercept the gypsies transporting Dracula's coffin.
